title: Parallelize weight hydration and isolate lexicon service to reduce startup tail latency
creator: Maya Chen
description:
Problem: Model boot and first-inference requests show a long tail (p95/p99) due to synchronous weight hydration and blocking tokenizer initialization tied directly into the model process. Multiple customers and internal benchmarks show spikes of 2-8s on cold-starts for large models. This ticket decouples lexicon/tokenizer responsibilities into a lightweight service and introduces a parallel, chunked weight hydration flow with an async handoff so model workers can accept requests earlier and finish activation in the background.

Goals: reduce cold-start p95 by 50% and p99 by 40% on the workloads in runtime-1.20 benchmark suite; avoid regressions in memory and runtime CPU; keep correctness for KV cache and tokenizer-vocab mapping during staged activation.

Non-goals: this ticket does not change checkpoint on-disk formats or introduce new model serialization formats; it focuses on runtime activation flow and tokenizer separation only.
acceptance_criteria: Cold-start p95 reduced by >=50% on the representative benchmark (same model/seq lengths used in runtime-1.20 tests)
Model worker process is able to accept and begin processing low-latency requests before full weight hydration completes (observed in traces)
Tokenizer/vocab lookups are served correctly during staged activation with zero correctness regressions on canonical prompt sets
Memory overhead increase <5% relative to current baseline during activation
End-to-end integration tests and canary rollout plan documented and executed
tech_notes: Design: introduce a Lexicon Gateway process that owns tokenizer initialization and vocab shard queries. Model workers start with a lightweight tokenizer stub that proxies lookups to the gateway until local vocab shard is available.
Hydration: implement chunked hydration where weight files are split into 8-32MB activation chunks; chunks are streamed with priority for attention and embedding layers first, followed by MLP blocks.
Activation protocol: model worker exposes a small activation API that accepts chunk metadata and applies atomic patching with validation checksums. Hydration client supports resume and backpressure.
Consistency: ensure KV cache priming waits for the layers it depends on; use a per-layer readiness vector and expose it in telemetry so router can choose fallback policies until ready.
Fallback: if lexicon gateway is unreachable, the worker falls back to bundled minimal vocab (subword fallback table) and emits degraded-mode metrics; automatic rollback path included in canary.
Performance trade-offs: parallel hydration increases peak IO; pair with adaptive rate limiter to protect shared storage and avoid noisy neighbor effects.

Compatibility: no on-disk checkpoint format changes; hydration chunks are a runtime transport concept only. Works with existing shard formats by reading ranges from weight files and mapping to chunk descriptors.
progress_updates: 2025-02-14 - Maya Chen created ticket with initial proposal and benchmark numbers.
2025-02-17 - Spike completed: prototype Lexicon Gateway that answers vocab queries over gRPC. Verified <1ms avg lookup when co-located on same host. - Owen Patel

2025-02-20 - Implemented chunked hydration prototype in runtime branch feat/chunk-hydration. Can stream and apply chunk 0..N. Observed 60% reduction in p95 in local sim for a 30B model when attention layers are prioritized. - Owen Patel

2025-02-24 - Design review with Infra and Storage: agreed on chunk size defaults (16MB) and backpressure lanes. Action: add adaptive IO limiter and add telemetry for activation bandwidth. - Reviewers: Lina Garcia, Priya Menon

2025-02-28 - Began integration tests: added activation readiness vector to test harness and wrote canary playbook. Blocker discovered: existing weight manifest lacks per-layer byte ranges for some legacy checkpoints; follow-up migration task created.
notes: Follow-up tasks: 1) add migration tool to annotate legacy weight manifests with layer byte ranges (separate ticket), 2) add operator visibility in Console for activation state per worker, 3) explore using local SSD cache warmers for heavy workloads.
